gen-gf-goldman-gf-yaldevi: Goldman spreads wide, bold letters with round forms like open parentheses. Yaldevi answers with oversized lowercase and an e that opens clearly to the right, which is the quality that holds the pair together.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-ubuntu-sans: Distinctive is Gugi's whole game, with tall lowercase nearly touching the capitals and terminals cut open. And Ubuntu Sans does the opposite job best, giving big-eyed lowercase and tubular strokes like bent copper pipe.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-vend-san: Love Ya Like A Sister keeps its ascenders barely above the x-height, with terminal tips flicking outward in an expressive, bold hand. Vend Sans, ruler-drawn and constant in width, is the pair's strongest card.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk keeps its e and a wide open with tall bowls. Grandstander does best with a bold, unvarying line and short ascenders, while the sans-serif body does best at holding terminals open and approachable.
gen-gf-tektur-fs-bespoke-sans: Tektur's strokes look like bent pipe cleaners, built from rods rather than carved blades, with tall outsized lowercase. The standout quality is how much sharper and lower Bespoke Sans feels beside it.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-abeezee: Expressive pipe-cleaner strokes give Tektur its character, with generous openings on every curve and outsized lowercase. And ABeeZee, a sans with neon-glass thickness and terminals finishing well clear of the stem, is what makes the pair approachable.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-aldrich: Pipe-cleaner strokes, wide-open curves, oversized lowercase: that is Tektur. Aldrich then carries a longer passage in cupped round letters with a tall x-height, like tracing one thick thread.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-alexandria: Tektur's pipe-cleaner strokes carry no calligraphic swell on any downstroke, and every curve opens generously. Alexandria, a clean sans-serif with a tall body and short stems, gives that angular energy a steadier partner underneath.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-amiko: Amiko brings modern lowercase strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark, with terminals pointing outward like tongs, against Tektur's rod-cut letters. Both keep one width.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-anek-bangla: Tektur's single-weight, pipe-cleaner strokes and outsized lowercase are what you notice first. And Anek Bangla, a sans-serif with wide s curves and a short rise from midline to ascender, reads smoothly over a longer stretch.
